answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds.. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. Consider a saffron as the anchor of the cost.
